_comment: The 'Did You Know?' column: true facts about the game world, by topic. Each edition prints a random selection. Keep each fact one or two short sentences, written as plain fact for the residents of the world.

Mobs: Creepers are afraid of cats and ocelots, and keep their distance from them.
A creeper struck by lightning becomes a charged creeper, and its explosion is far more powerful.
A mob killed by a charged creeper's explosion drops its head.
Endermen take damage from water and rain, and teleport away from it.
Looking an enderman in the eye provokes it, unless you are wearing a carved pumpkin.
Endermen pick up certain blocks, such as grass, dirt, sand, flowers, melons and pumpkins.
Skeletons and zombies burn in daylight unless they wear a helmet or find shade or water.
Spiders are neutral in bright light and hostile in the dark.
Spiders can climb walls. A spider ridden by a skeleton is called a spider jockey.
Baby zombies are fast, fit through one-block gaps and never grow up.
A baby zombie riding a chicken is known as a chicken jockey.
Zombies can turn villagers into zombie villagers, especially on harder difficulties.
A zombie villager can be cured with a splash potion of weakness and a golden apple.
Cured zombie villagers give the player who cured them large trade discounts.
A zombie that stays underwater long enough turns into a drowned.
Some drowned carry tridents, and they are the only source of tridents.
Husks live in deserts and do not burn in sunlight.
Strays live in snowy biomes and shoot arrows of slowness.
A skeleton stuck in powder snow eventually turns into a stray.
Witches drink potions to heal themselves and to resist fire.
A villager struck by lightning turns into a witch.
A pig struck by lightning turns into a zombified piglin.
A mooshroom struck by lightning changes between red and brown.
Feeding a flower to a brown mooshroom lets you milk it for suspicious stew.
Sheep regrow their wool by eating grass.
A sheep named jeb_ cycles through every wool colour, though it still drops its own.
Naming a mob Dinnerbone or Grumm turns it upside down.
A rabbit named Toast gets a special black-and-white coat.
A vindicator named Johnny attacks almost every mob it sees.
Iron golems sometimes offer a poppy to villagers.
Snow golems leave a trail of snow and take damage in hot biomes and rain.
Shearing a snow golem removes its pumpkin head.
Tamed cats sometimes bring their owners gifts in the morning, such as rabbit hide or phantom membrane.
Phantoms come for players who have not slept for three in-game days.
Phantoms are afraid of cats.
Parrots dance when a jukebox plays nearby.
Parrots imitate the sounds of nearby hostile mobs.
Feeding a parrot a cookie is deadly to it.
Foxes carry items in their mouths and swap them for something they like better.
A fox kit bred by a player trusts that player.
Axolotls help players fight underwater mobs, and play dead to recover when hurt.
Blue axolotls are rare: about one in every 1,200 bred babies.
Goats ram players and mobs, sometimes right off a cliff.
A goat that rams a solid block can drop a goat horn.
Screaming goats are a rare variant with louder, stranger noises.
Wardens are blind and track players by sound and smell.
A warden has 500 health, more than twice the Ender Dragon's 200.
Wardens are summoned by sculk shriekers in the deep dark.
Allays collect items that match the one they are holding.
An allay given an amethyst shard while it dances to a jukebox duplicates itself.
Sniffer eggs are found by brushing suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins.
Sniffers dig up ancient seeds: the torchflower and the pitcher pod.
Camels carry two riders and are tall enough that many mobs cannot reach them.
Armadillos roll into a ball when threatened, and drop scutes used for wolf armour.
Breezes live in trial chambers and deflect most projectiles.
Breezes drop breeze rods, which are crafted into wind charges.
The bogged is a mossy skeleton that shoots poisoned arrows.
A creaking cannot be hurt for good; only breaking its creaking heart stops it.
A creaking only moves while no player is looking at it.
A bee dies some time after stinging a player.
Bees carrying pollen help nearby crops grow.
A campfire under a beehive lets you collect honey without angering the bees.
Turtles always return to their home beach to lay eggs.
Baby turtles drop a turtle scute when they grow up.
Dolphins fed raw fish lead players towards shipwrecks and ruins.
Swimming beside a dolphin gives you Dolphin's Grace, a burst of speed.
Pufferfish puff up and poison anything that comes too close.
Glow squid drop glow ink sacs, which make the writing on signs glow.
Llamas spit at hostile mobs and at players who hit them.
Wandering traders arrive with two trader llamas.
Every horse has its own speed, jump strength and health.
Skeleton horses appear in skeleton traps during thunderstorms.
Striders walk on lava, and shiver and slow down when out of it.
Hoglins are afraid of warped fungus.
Piglins love gold and barter items in exchange for gold ingots.
Piglins attack players who are not wearing at least one piece of gold armour.
Piglins and hoglins brought to the Overworld turn into zombified versions.
A ghast's fireball can be punched or shot back at it.
Killing a ghast with its own fireball earns the advancement Return to Sender.
Magma cubes split into smaller magma cubes when killed.
Slimes spawn in swamps at night and deep underground in slime chunks.
Shulkers hide in their shells and fire bullets that make you levitate.
Shulkers are found in End cities.
The Ender Dragon heals itself using the End crystals on top of the obsidian pillars.
The first Ender Dragon defeated drops 12,000 experience points; later ones drop 500.
The Wither is built from soul sand and three wither skeleton skulls.
The Wither drops a Nether star, the key ingredient of a beacon.
Endermites sometimes appear where a thrown ender pearl lands.
Silverfish hide inside infested stone blocks.
Elder guardians give nearby players Mining Fatigue.
Evokers summon vexes, which fly straight through walls.
Evokers drop the totem of undying.
Polar bears are protective of their cubs.
Every panda has a personality: some are lazy, worried, playful, aggressive or weak.
Brown pandas are the rarest kind of panda.
A thrown egg has a one in eight chance of hatching a chick.
A frog's colour depends on the biome its tadpole grew up in.
Frogs that eat small magma cubes leave behind a froglight.
Tadpoles can be scooped up and carried in a bucket of water.
Wolves are tamed with bones, and come in several coats depending on their biome.
Tamed wolves will not attack creepers.
Zombified piglins are neutral until one of them is attacked; then the whole group joins in.
Vindicators swing axes, and are found in woodland mansions and raids.
Ravagers join raids and can knock down leaves and crops in their way.
Cave spiders are smaller than spiders and poison their targets.
Bats hang upside down from cave ceilings while they rest.
Squid flee from players and release a cloud of ink when hurt.
Redstone: A redstone signal travels up to 15 blocks along dust before it needs a repeater.
Repeaters can delay a signal by one to four redstone ticks.
A redstone tick lasts a tenth of a second: two game ticks.
Comparators can measure how full a chest, barrel or other container is.
A comparator with its front torch lit subtracts its side signal from its rear one.
Observers send out a pulse when the block in front of them changes.
A piston can push up to 12 blocks at once.
Slime and honey blocks drag neighbouring blocks along when moved by a piston.
Slime blocks and honey blocks do not stick to each other.
Obsidian, bedrock and reinforced deepslate cannot be moved by pistons.
Pistons cannot move chests, furnaces or other blocks that store items.
Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime or honey blocks.
A redstone torch turns off when the block it is attached to is powered.
A redstone torch flickered on and off too quickly burns out for a while.
Clicking a daylight detector switches it to detecting night instead.
A target block gives a stronger signal the closer a projectile lands to its centre.
Sculk sensors detect vibrations up to eight blocks away.
Wool blocks stop vibrations from reaching sculk sensors.
Calibrated sculk sensors can listen for one kind of vibration only.
Hoppers move two and a half items every second.
A hopper powered by redstone stops moving items.
Dispensers can place water, shoot arrows, light TNT and put armour on players.
A dispenser holding shears will shear a sheep standing in front of it.
Note blocks play a different instrument depending on the block beneath them.
A note block has 25 pitches, changed by right-clicking it.
A lectern gives a signal based on which page of its book is open.
An item frame gives a comparator signal based on how its item is turned.
Copper bulbs switch on or off with each redstone pulse they receive.
The crafter crafts an item each time it receives a redstone pulse.
Tripwire hooks give a signal when anything passes through their string.
Stone pressure plates only notice players and mobs; wooden ones notice items and arrows too.
Weighted pressure plates give a stronger signal the more things are on them.
Lit TNT explodes after four seconds.
TNT can be lit by redstone, fire, flaming arrows or another explosion.
Powered rails speed minecarts up when powered and brake them when not.
Detector rails give a signal when a minecart rolls over them.
Activator rails can light TNT minecarts and throw riders out of their carts.
A bell rung by redstone makes nearby raiders glow.
Redstone lamps only light up while powered.
Pistons can be powered by a block diagonally above them, an old quirk known as quasi-connectivity.
A lightning rod gives a redstone signal when struck.
A trapped chest gives a redstone signal while it is open.
A jukebox gives a signal while playing, and a comparator can tell which disc it is.
Redstone blocks are a power source that never turns off.
Levers stay on or off; buttons give a short pulse and then switch off.
Wooden buttons stay pressed longer than stone ones, and can be pressed by arrows.
Blocks: Bedrock cannot be broken in Survival.
Obsidian forms where water flows onto a lava source.
Mining obsidian takes a diamond pickaxe or better.
Ancient debris shrugs off explosions, which is why miners use beds and TNT to find it.
Ancient debris is most common around Y level 15 in the Nether.
Diamonds are most common deep underground, well below Y 0.
Sand, gravel, concrete powder and anvils fall if nothing is beneath them.
Concrete powder turns into solid concrete when it touches water.
Ice melts near bright light, but packed ice and blue ice never melt.
Blue ice is so slippery that boats on it travel faster than almost anything.
Soul sand slows down anything walking across it.
Magma blocks hurt anything that walks on them, unless it is sneaking.
Soul sand under water makes a bubble column that pushes upwards; magma pulls downwards.
A wet sponge dries in a furnace, or instantly when placed in the Nether.
Glass breaks into nothing unless it is mined with Silk Touch.
Leaves decay when there is no log within six blocks of them.
Grass spreads to nearby dirt as long as there is enough light.
Beds explode when used in the Nether or the End.
Respawn anchors explode when used outside the Nether.
A respawn anchor is charged with glowstone and holds up to four charges.
A full four-layer beacon pyramid takes 164 blocks of iron, gold, emerald, diamond or netherite.
A conduit gives nearby players underwater breathing, night vision and faster mining.
Torches placed around a spawner stop most mobs spawning from it.
Budding amethyst cannot be picked up, even with Silk Touch.
Pointed dripstone above a cauldron slowly fills it with water or lava.
A whole tower of scaffolding falls when its bottom piece is broken.
Honey blocks slow falls and let players slide slowly down their sides.
Slime blocks bounce anything that lands on them.
Cobwebs slow everything down, and swords cut through them quickly.
A campfire cooks up to four pieces of food at once.
Soul fire burns blue, and piglins keep away from soul torches and soul lanterns.
Sea lanterns drop prismarine crystals unless mined with Silk Touch.
Copper slowly turns green as it oxidises, unless it is waxed with honeycomb.
A lightning strike scrapes the oxidation off nearby copper.
An axe scrapes oxidation or wax off copper blocks.
A chiseled bookshelf holds six books.
Decorated pots are made from bricks and pottery sherds found by archaeology.
Suspicious sand and gravel must be brushed to reveal what is inside.
Crying obsidian is used to craft respawn anchors.
A lodestone makes any compass used on it point back to it.
Composters turn seeds, leaves and other plants into bone meal.
Jack o'lanterns give light underwater, unlike torches.
Sea pickles glow underwater, more brightly in groups.
Mud is made by pouring a water bottle onto dirt.
Mud placed above pointed dripstone slowly dries into clay.
Snow layers stack up to eight high.
Powder snow swallows anyone who steps in, unless they wear leather boots.
Staying in powder snow too long makes you freeze.
Landing on a hay bale reduces fall damage by 80 percent.
Landing in water cancels fall damage completely.
Sweet berry bushes hurt anything that walks through them.
Cacti destroy items that touch them.
Wither roses give the Wither effect to anything that touches them.
A dragon egg teleports away when hit.
There is only one dragon egg in each world.
A chest cannot be opened with a solid block, or a sitting cat, on top of it.
Every ender chest opens the same storage for the same player.
Shulker boxes keep their contents when they are broken.
Barrels can be opened even with a block on top of them.
Glowstone drops two to four glowstone dust when broken.
Tinted glass lets no light through at all.
A furnace smelts one item every ten seconds; a blast furnace or smoker is twice as fast.
A bucket of lava keeps a furnace burning for 100 items.
A block of coal burns in a furnace for as long as ten pieces of coal.
Dried kelp blocks and bamboo both work as furnace fuel.
Netherrack burns forever once lit.
Items: Netherite items do not burn in lava or fire.
Upgrading to netherite takes a smithing template found in bastion remnants.
Smithing templates can be copied using diamonds and the right material.
A totem of undying held in either hand saves you from death once.
Ender pearls teleport the thrower to where they land, with a little fall damage.
Elytra are found on the End ships beside some End cities.
Elytra are repaired with phantom membranes.
Firework rockets give a burst of speed to a player flying with elytra.
A trident with Riptide launches its thrower, but only in water or rain.
A trident with Channeling summons lightning during a thunderstorm.
Maps can be copied and locked at a cartography table.
A spyglass lets you zoom in on far-off things.
A recovery compass points to where you last died.
Clocks show the time of day, and spin wildly in the Nether and the End.
A normal compass points to the world's spawn point.
Enchanted golden apples cannot be crafted, only found in chests.
A cake has seven slices.
Eating rotten flesh may give you the Hunger effect.
A suspicious stew's effect depends on the flower it was made with.
Drinking milk clears every status effect.
A honey bottle cures poison.
Eating chorus fruit teleports you to a random nearby spot.
Golden carrots are one of the most filling foods in the game.
Dried kelp is eaten faster than almost any other food.
Shields block arrows and explosions, but an axe can knock them out of use.
Crossbows can be loaded with firework rockets.
A bow with Infinity needs only one arrow in your inventory.
Mending repairs an item using the experience you collect.
Mending and Infinity cannot be on the same bow.
Silk Touch and Fortune cannot be on the same tool.
Fortune III can turn one diamond ore into as many as four diamonds.
Looting makes mobs drop more of their loot.
Frost Walker turns water into ice under your feet as you walk.
Soul Speed is only found in bastion chests and piglin bartering.
Swift Sneak is only found in ancient city chests.
The mace hits harder the further you fall before striking.
The mace is crafted from a heavy core and a breeze rod.
A wind charge thrown at your feet launches you into the air.
A bundle holds a mix of different items in one slot.
A brush uncovers items hidden in suspicious sand and gravel.
The music disc Pigstep is only found in bastion remnants.
A creeper killed by a skeleton's arrow drops a music disc.
The music disc 5 is pieced together from nine fragments found in ancient cities.
Goat horns come in eight different sounds.
A lead can tie an animal to a fence post.
Fishing sometimes reels in treasure, such as enchanted books, bows and name tags.
Luck of the Sea makes fishing treasure more likely.
A turtle shell helmet gives ten seconds of extra breathing underwater.
Shears turn a pumpkin into a carved pumpkin.
A written book can be copied by crafting it with a book and quill.
Swords can sweep, hitting several mobs at once.
Animals killed with Fire Aspect drop cooked meat.
Armour trims change how armour looks, and come from smithing templates found around the world.
An iron golem is repaired by right-clicking it with an iron ingot.
Bottles o' enchanting burst into experience orbs when thrown.
Glow item frames make the item inside them shine in the dark.
Sticky pistons are made by adding a slimeball to a piston.
A heart of the sea is used to craft a conduit.
An eye of ender floats towards the nearest stronghold when thrown.
The World: A full day in the world lasts 20 minutes of real time.
The world stretches about 30 million blocks from its centre in every direction.
The Overworld runs from Y -64 at the bottom to Y 320 at the build limit.
Each block travelled in the Nether covers eight blocks in the Overworld.
The Nether has a bedrock roof, with nothing natural above it.
Water poured in the Nether boils away at once.
Lava flows faster and further in the Nether than in the Overworld.
The moon has eight phases, one for each night of its cycle.
Slimes spawn in swamps most often under a full moon.
Mobs are more likely to wear armour and carry weapons on harder difficulties.
Mushroom fields are the only biome where hostile mobs never spawn on their own.
The deep dark lies far below the surface, often beneath mountains.
Ancient cities in the deep dark hold rare loot, such as Swift Sneak books.
Woodland mansions are rare and guarded by vindicators and evokers.
Every ocean monument hides eight blocks of gold.
Each world has 128 strongholds.
An End portal needs 12 eyes of ender to light.
Each End portal frame has a one in ten chance of already holding an eye.
A thrown eye of ender sometimes breaks instead of dropping.
Desert temples hide a TNT trap under a pressure plate.
Jungle temples are guarded by tripwires and arrow traps.
Buried treasure chests always hold a heart of the sea.
Shipwrecks often carry buried treasure maps.
Trial chamber vaults open with trial keys won from trial spawners.
Ominous trial spawners appear when a player with Trial Omen comes near.
Villages come in five styles: plains, desert, savanna, taiga and snowy.
Lightning rods attract nearby lightning and protect flammable roofs.
Hostile mobs can spawn in daylight during a thunderstorm.
Beds can only be slept in at night or during a thunderstorm.
Pale gardens hide creaking hearts inside their pale oak trees.
Cherry groves have pink-leaved trees that scatter pink petals.
Mangrove swamps are home to frogs, mud and mangrove roots.
Lush caves are full of glow berries, moss and axolotls.
The same world seed always generates the same world.
Amethyst geodes are found underground, wrapped in smooth basalt and calcite.
Nether wart grows in Nether fortresses and bastion remnants.
Blazes are found only in Nether fortresses.
Bastion remnants hold blocks of gold and are guarded by piglins and piglin brutes.
Some End cities have an End ship floating beside them, with elytra on board.
The End's outer islands are reached through End gateways.
Fossils made of bone blocks are buried beneath deserts and swamps.
It snows instead of raining in cold biomes and high up on mountains.
Trail ruins are half-buried ruins full of suspicious gravel to dig through.
Igloos sometimes hide a secret basement with a zombie villager and a cleric.
Pillager outposts are watchtowers guarded by pillagers.
Ruined portals are broken Nether portals found in both the Overworld and the Nether.
Dripstone caves are full of stalactites and stalagmites made of pointed dripstone.
The End is reached through the portal in a stronghold.
Villagers: A villager takes its profession from the job site block it claims, such as a composter for a farmer.
Once you trade with a villager, its profession is fixed.
Librarians work at lecterns and sell enchanted books.
Villagers restock their trades up to twice a day at their job site.
Villagers breed when they have enough food and free beds.
Villagers sleep at night and gather around the village bell.
Defeating a raid earns the Hero of the Village effect, with discounts and gifts.
Nitwits have no job and wear green coats.
Baby villagers run around the village playing.
Villagers lower their prices for players with a good reputation.
Hurting a villager makes its prices go up.
Villagers who see a zombie panic, and may call an iron golem to help.
Wandering traders drink invisibility potions at night and leave after a while.
Cartographers sell explorer maps that lead to ocean monuments and woodland mansions.
Clerics buy rotten flesh.
Fletchers buy sticks.
Masons buy clay.
Villagers wear clothes that match the biome they come from.
Farmer villagers harvest and replant crops, and share food with other villagers.
A villager's badge shows its level: stone, iron, gold, emerald and diamond.
A raid begins when a player with Bad Omen walks into a village.
Armorers, toolsmiths and weaponsmiths will buy coal and iron.
A villager without a bed cannot breed.
Shepherds work at looms; leatherworkers at cauldrons; butchers at smokers.
Brewing and Enchanting: Most potions start as an awkward potion: a water bottle brewed with nether wart.
One piece of blaze powder fuels a brewing stand for 20 brews.
Redstone makes a potion last longer; glowstone makes it stronger.
A fermented spider eye reverses many potions: swiftness becomes slowness.
Gunpowder turns a potion into a splash potion; dragon's breath makes it lingering.
The potion of the Turtle Master gives Resistance and Slowness at the same time.
A potion of weakness is brewed from a water bottle and a fermented spider eye, without nether wart.
Phantom membrane brews a potion of slow falling.
A pufferfish brews a potion of water breathing.
A golden carrot brews a potion of night vision.
A rabbit's foot brews a potion of leaping.
A ghast tear brews a potion of regeneration.
Magma cream brews a potion of fire resistance.
A glistering melon slice brews a potion of healing.
An enchanting table needs 15 bookshelves around it to offer level 30 enchantments.
Bookshelves must be one block away from the enchanting table, with nothing in between.
Enchanting takes lapis lazuli as well as experience.
Each time an item is worked on an anvil, the next repair costs more.
An anvil job costing 40 levels or more is too expensive in Survival.
A grindstone removes enchantments, except curses, and gives back some experience.
Curse of Binding stops armour being taken off.
Curse of Vanishing makes an item disappear when you die.
Thorns damages anything that hits the wearer.
Protection IV is the strongest protection an enchanting table can give.
Wind Burst on a mace launches you back into the air after a hit.
Density and Breach are enchantments for the mace only.
Ominous bottles give the Bad Omen effect.
Potions of Oozing, Weaving and Wind Charged release slimes, cobwebs or a burst of wind when their drinker dies.
A potion of invisibility is made by adding a fermented spider eye to a potion of night vision.
Splash potions of healing hurt undead mobs, and potions of harming heal them.
Farming: Wheat seeds are found by breaking grass.
Crops need a light level of at least nine to grow.
Bone meal makes crops, saplings and flowers grow faster.
Farmland turns back into dirt when something jumps on it.
Sugar cane must be planted right next to water.
Cocoa beans grow on the side of jungle logs.
Pumpkins and melons grow from a stem onto a neighbouring block.
Cows are bred with wheat, pigs with carrots, potatoes or beetroot, and chickens with seeds.
A sheep dyed before shearing gives wool of that colour.
Farmland stays moist when there is water within four blocks.
Nether wart only grows on soul sand.
Chorus plants only grow on end stone.
Bamboo can grow more than 12 blocks tall.
Bees make honey faster when there are plenty of flowers nearby.
Cactus needs sand to grow, and nothing solid beside it.
Kelp grows upwards from the sea floor until it reaches the surface.
Survival: A critical hit lands when you strike while falling.
Waiting for the attack bar to refill makes each hit land at full strength.
Axes hit harder than swords, but swing more slowly.
You need more than three drumsticks of hunger to sprint.
Health slowly comes back while the hunger bar is nearly full.
Dying drops only part of your experience.
Sneaking stops you falling off the edge of a block.
Swimming is faster than walking through water.
Boats are one of the fastest ways to travel on water and ice.
Placing water at the bottom of a drop makes the fall safe.
Lava can set nearby flammable blocks alight without touching them.
History: The game was first shown to the public in May 2009.
The creeper began as a mistake: a pig model built with its height and length swapped.
The Nether arrived in 2010, in the Halloween Update.
The End and the Ender Dragon arrived with version 1.0 in November 2011.
Herobrine is listed as removed in many update notes, as a running joke.
The title screen's yellow splash text has hundreds of possible messages.
The original soundtrack was composed by C418.
Update Aquatic (1.13) brought dolphins, the drowned and coral reefs.
Village and Pillage (1.14) rebuilt villagers and introduced raids.
The Nether Update (1.16) added netherite, piglins and four new Nether biomes.
Caves and Cliffs (1.17 and 1.18) took the world down to Y -64.
The Wild Update (1.19) added the warden, the deep dark and frogs.
Trails and Tales (1.20) added archaeology, camels and cherry groves.
Tricky Trials (1.21) added trial chambers, the breeze and the mace.
The Garden Awakens added the pale garden and the creaking.
The phantom won the first mob vote, in 2017.
The glow squid, the allay, the sniffer and the armadillo were all chosen by players in mob votes.
It is the best-selling video game of all time.
